title: Fire and Ice
book: NCERT First Flight: Textbook in English for Class X
subject: english_literature
author: Robert Frost
syllabus_note: CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184): First Flight poem 2. Assessed through poetry extracts (5 marks) and short answers (3 marks); can appear in long answers.

blocks.title: Fire or ice?
blocks.body: Scientists have argued about whether the world will end in a great **fire** or in a frozen **ice** age. In nine short lines, **Robert Frost** turns this question inward: the real fire and ice are **inside us**: desire and hatred.

blocks.title: The poet
blocks.body: **Robert Frost**, four-time Pulitzer Prize winner, published Fire and Ice in **1920**. The poem is short, but each word is chosen with care.
blocks.future: Poems like this train us to read symbols, a skill used in literature, advertising, film and law.

blocks.question: Why might hatred be compared to ice rather than to fire?
options: Hatred is cold, rigid and slowly destroys relationships
blocks.explanation: Ice suggests coldness, indifference and rigidity.

blocks.title: Fire and Ice
blocks.body:
*Some say the world will end in fire,*
*Some say in ice.*
*From what I've tasted of desire*
*I hold with those who favour fire.*
*But if it had to perish twice,*
*I think I know enough of hate*
*To say that for destruction ice*
*Is also great*
*And would suffice.*

blocks.title: What the poem says
blocks.body:
**Lines 1-2:** some people believe the world will end in **fire**, others in **ice**.

**Lines 3-4:** from his experience of **desire**, the poet agrees with those who favour fire. Fire stands for **desire**: greed, lust, ambition and fury, which spread quickly and burn out of control.

**Lines 5-9:** but if the world had to be destroyed **twice**, he knows enough about **hate** to say that ice would also be great for destruction and 'would **suffice**' (be enough). Ice stands for **hatred**: coldness, indifference, rigidity and intolerance, which destroy slowly.

**Message:** human emotions such as uncontrolled desire and hatred can destroy the world.

blocks.title: Fire and ice as symbols
blocks.body:
| Symbol | Stands for | How it destroys |
|---|---|---|
| **Fire** | desire: greed, avarice, lust, conflict, fury | spreads quickly and burns everything |
| **Ice** | hatred: cruelty, intolerance, rigidity, insensitivity, coldness, indifference | slowly freezes relationships and kills feeling |

blocks.question: What does 'fire' stand for in the poem?
blocks.explanation: From what he has tasted of desire, he favours fire.

blocks.question: What does 'suffice' mean?
blocks.explanation: Ice would be enough to destroy the world.

blocks.title: How the form supports the idea
blocks.body:
**Rhyme scheme:** **aba abc bcb** (fire/desire/fire; ice/twice/ice/suffice; hate/great). The rhymes link the two opposite ideas, fire and ice, and the poem swings between them.

**Short last lines:** 'Is also great / And would suffice' are very short, ending the poem with a cold, quiet, chilling force.

**Symbolism and irony:** simple words carry deep meaning; the casual tone ('Some say... I think I know enough...') makes the warning more powerful.

**Contrast:** fire (hot, fast) against ice (cold, slow): both destroy.

blocks.title: Memory tricks
blocks.body:
- **Fire = Desire (both end in -ire!). Ice = hate (cold).**
- **9 lines; rhyme aba abc bcb; perish twice.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. Reading the poem as only about science: it is about **human emotions**.
2. Saying the poet favours ice: he **holds with fire**, but says ice is also great.
3. Mixing the symbols: fire = desire, ice = hate.

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: List twelve words (greed, avarice, cruelty, lust, conflict, fury, intolerance, rigidity, insensitivity, coldness, indifference, hatred). Students sort them into Fire or Ice and explain.

blocks.title: Think and explain
blocks.body: Which do you think harms the world more today, greed or hatred? Give one example.

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Dust of Snow:** another short Frost poem.
- **Nelson Mandela:** how hatred is learnt and can be unlearnt.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
'Fire and Ice' is a warning about human nature. Explain in about 120 words.

**Model answer:** On the surface Frost repeats a debate about whether the world will end in fire or in ice. But he uses these as symbols of human emotions. Fire stands for desire: greed, lust and ambition that spread quickly and burn everything. From his own experience of desire, he agrees the world could end in fire. Ice stands for hatred: cold, rigid indifference that slowly destroys relationships. He says that if the world had to perish twice, ice would 'suffice' too. The calm tone and short final lines make the warning chilling. The poem tells us that if we do not control our desires and our hatred, we ourselves may destroy the world.

blocks.title: Summary
blocks.body:
- Some say the world will end in fire, some in ice.
- Fire symbolises desire; ice symbolises hatred.
- Either is powerful enough to destroy the world; the poem warns us to control both.

blocks.title: Exam tips
blocks.body:
- Always explain both symbols.
- Mention the rhyme scheme and how it links the contrasting ideas.
- Quote 'would suffice' for the power of hatred.

blocks.front: What do fire and ice symbolise?
blocks.back: Fire: desire (greed, lust). Ice: hatred (coldness, indifference).
